title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' manuscript, a sequel to La Longue Marche, so it belongs to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller circle. Grothendieck pushes the loop equation for elements of a group N_{0,3}^{!~} into the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ) / GL(2,Ẑ).

Setting.
- Π_{0,3}, the fundamental group of P^1 minus 3 points, is realised as the principal congruence subgroup Γ(2), modulo ±1.
- Its profinite completion Π̂_{0,3} maps to SL(2,Ẑ). The image of an element is written as a 2×2 matrix over Ẑ.
- ℓ_0 = [[1,2],[0,1]] and ℓ_1 are the loop generators.
- ρ is conjugation by an order-3 element and σ_∞ is conjugation by an order-2 element (order 4 in SL_2).
- μ ∈ Ẑ^* is the cyclotomic-type parameter. ε_2(μ) = ±1 is the sign with μ ≡ ε_2 (mod 4); ε_3(μ) is the sign with μ ≡ ε_3 (mod 3).

Proposition (previous page). Write α = [[a,b],[c,d]] and β = [[r,s],[t,u]]. Require det α = ε_3, det β = 1, and the loop relation α ρ(α)^{-1} = ε_2 (β σ_∞(β)^{-1}) ℓ_1^ν with ν = (μ−1)/2. Such α, β exist iff (88) holds: ε_3(c²+cd+d²) = ε_2(t²+u²) = 1/μ.
- The two binary forms are the norm forms of Z[ω] and Z[i]. They appear because the stabilisers relevant to ρ and σ_∞ are the tori given by the centralisers of the order-3 and order-4 elements.
- The bottom rows (c,d), (t,u) are the invariant data. The top rows are only defined up to left multiplication by the upper unipotent ℓ_0^n, which preserves bottom rows.
- The solution set is a Ẑ-torsor under (α,β) ↦ (ℓ_0^n α, ℓ_0^n β).

This page.
- It finishes that statement; the word 'Exercice' at the top is struck out.
- Corollary: one can additionally require α ≡ β ≡ 1 (mod 2), i.e. land in the image of Π̂_{0,3}, iff c ≡ t ≡ 0 and d ≡ u ≡ 1 (mod 2). The solutions satisfying this form a Ẑ-torsor under the same ℓ_0^n action. This is consistent because ℓ_0 ≡ 1 (mod 2).
- Scholie: an element of N_{0,3}^{!~} determines α, β only modulo this ℓ_0-action. So its intrinsic data are the 'adelic invariants' Θ = (μ, c, d, t, u), with (c,d,t,u) subject to (88) and determined only up to some ambiguity. Grothendieck says this is the best one can do as long as a, b, r, s have no intrinsic characterisation: they are not invariants.
- For an actual (effective) automorphism, one also has a canonical lift f ∈ SL(2,Ẑ)', hence f ∈ Π̂_{0,3}. It is written f = [[g,k],[l,m]] and is defined modulo (probably) ±1 and modulo f ↦ ℓ_0^n f.

Next page. He tries to repackage (α,β,f) as a point of the contracted product Ť_Θ ∧^{Ẑ} SL(2,Ẑ), a right SL(2,Ẑ)-torsor. From it he wants to recover the image of the automorphism in GL(2,Ẑ)'. He then admits the formulation is 'not enthusing'.

Aim. To classify the congruence-level (SL_2(Ẑ)) shadow of GT-type automorphisms by explicit adelic invariants.
errors: Consistency check for (88) and the corollary. With c even, d odd: c²+cd+d² ≡ 1 (mod 2). With t even, u odd: t²+u² ≡ 1 (mod 4), so ε_2(t²+u²) = μ^{-1} forces μ ≡ ε_2 (mod 4), consistent with the definition of ε_2. When 3 does not divide both c and d, c²+cd+d² ≡ 1 (mod 3), giving μ ≡ ε_3 (mod 3), consistent with ε_3.
The ambiguity in (c,d,t,u) is left vague: 'déterminés aux ... près'.
Notational clash: 'u' denotes both the element of N_{0,3}^{!~} and the matrix entry of β, and the exponent written 'u' in ℓ_0^u should be n.

ideas.what: Necessary and sufficient condition for solvability of the loop equation in SL/GL(2,Ẑ): bottom rows must represent 1/μ (up to the signs ε_3, ε_2) by the norm forms x²+xy+y² and x²+y²; the solution set is a Ẑ-torsor under left multiplication by ℓ_0^n
ideas.modern_name: congruence (SL_2(Ẑ)) image of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller / loop equations; tori Z[ω]^*, Z[i]^* as centralisers of elliptic elements
ideas.usually_credited_to: General GT framework: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura. This specific computation: not known in the literature.

ideas.what: Corollary: refinement to α ≡ β ≡ 1 mod 2 (landing in the image of Π̂_{0,3}), via parity conditions on c, d, t, u

Adelic invariants Θ = (μ, c, d, t, u) attached to an element of N_{0,3}^{!~}; the top rows a, b, r, s are recognised as non-invariant, and a torsor reformulation (contracted product Ť_Θ ∧^{Ẑ} SL(2,Ẑ)) follows on the next page
ideas.modern_name: torsor-theoretic description of the congruence image of GT elements

missed.claim: Grothendieck attaches to each GT-type element explicit adelic invariants (μ, c, d, t, u), constrained by representability of μ^{-1} by the Eisenstein and Gaussian norm forms. He wants to reconstruct the GL(2,Ẑ)-image from these plus a lift f, but finds the torsor formulation unsatisfying and leaves it.
missed.quote: il leur est attaché les "invariants adéliques" (90) Θ=(μ,c,d,t,u) ... et c'est ce qu'on peut faire de mieux tant que les a,b,r,s n'ont pas une caractérisation constructive
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives an explicit description of the image of GT (or its variants) in the congruence completion SL_2(Ẑ). The role of the order-3 and order-2 elliptic tori (norm forms of Z[ω], Z[i]) in the loop equations is not spelled out this way in the GT literature.

missed.claim: Solvability of the two GT relations at congruence level is tied to binary quadratic norm forms of Q(√−3) and Q(i), i.e. to the CM points of orders 3 and 2.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a modest link between GT relations and CM/elliptic-point arithmetic. It is likely easy for specialists to reconstruct, though.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but essentially elementary computation of the congruence shadow of the loop equations. It is unpublished and has a nice norm-form structure, but a specialist would find it natural rather than surprising.
transcription_corrections: Exponent 'ℓ_0^u' should read ℓ_0^n (lines 1, 10 and the inserted text in the Scholie).

The corollary's last sentence should read roughly 'et alors l'ensemble des solutions (α,β) satisfaisant à ces conditions supplémentaires est un torseur sous Ẑ', not 'l'une des solutions ... s'appliquent'.
'Exercice' at the end of line 1 is struck out.
(91): f is 'défini mod ±1 (?) et mod f ↦ ℓ_0^n f'; the transcribed 'défini mod tel que' is garbled.
The parenthesis after (90) is roughly '(c,d,t,u déterminés aux ambiguïtés près de ... satisfaisant (88) ...)'; the transcription duplicates text there.
